newsitem.title: UK: Vodafone firm after results, acquisition.
newsitem.headline: Vodafone firm after results, acquisition.

text.p: Shares in Vodafone Plc were firm on Tuesday after the mobile phone company posted first-half results towards the top end of the range of analyst estimates and said it was buying retailer Peoples Phone Plc.
The stock was up 4p at 247-1/2 by 1342 GMT, after being up just 1/2p shortly before the results and acquisition were announced.
Vodafone said pre-tax profit in the six months ended Septembr 30 rose to 21 percent 252.4 million stg, including a 17.2 million stg credit, from 206.2 million a year before.
That compares with analyst expectations of between 220 million stg and 250 million before exceptional credits.

Vodafone said it was paying 77 million stg for Peoples Phone, which would increase its existing current service provider business through the addition of Peoples Phone's 395,500 subscribers and its chain of 181 retail outlets.
"Vodafone rarely disappoints and it certainly hasn't this time around," said Evan Miller, analyst at CS First Boston.
"Rumours of the demise of the UK mobile 'phone market have proved premature, there is life in the market and Vodafone is taking more than its fair share of it."
Miller said results from Vodafone's international operations were promising, the dividend was at the top end of the range of forecasts, while cash flow and operating margins were also strong.

He said the Peoples Phone purchase was also positive. "They are trying to solidify their position as a service provider and retailer and the more subscribers they control either directly or indirectly the better."
By 1418 GMT,the stock was up 7-1/2p at 251 -- after rising as high as 252, its highest since July.
